valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 underlying EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), times a justified P/E, in USD per share. Listing is an ADR: the depositary (BNY Mellon) states each ADS represents one ordinary share (424B7 prospectus supplement, 2024; FY2025 20-F reiterates the 1:1 ratio), so the ADR ratio is 1:1 and per-share figures carry over without scaling. AB InBev reports in USD, so the valuation needs no FX conversion. FX is used only for EUR-quoted items: EUR/USD 1.1052 (Banque de France daily reference rate, 13 Nov 2026) converts the EUR 0.40 FY2026 interim dividend ($0.44) and the EUR-quoted Barclays target (EUR 82 and EUR 95 shown as $90.63 and $104.99; same rate applied to both, not the July 27 rate). Anchor: FY2025 underlying EPS $3.73; 9M26 underlying EPS $3.40 (vs $2.78 in 9M25, +22.2%, of which about 8 points FX per the constant-currency comparison); FY2026E about $4.45 = 9M actual plus an assumed Q4 of about $1.05 (Q4 2025 was $0.95 grown by roughly the 9M FX-inclusive rate; my estimate, not company guidance). Company guidance: EBITDA to grow in line with the 4-8% medium-term outlook; net capex $3.5-4.0bn; no EPS guidance. FY2027E EPS is my own assumption: no 2027 outlook was issued, and no sourced post-Q3 2027 consensus was found. Diluted share count taken from the 1,973M weighted average in 3Q26.

bear.driver: FX tailwind reverses and the 2027 Brazil sin tax (cited by Barclays) hits a large profit pool; the World Cup-supported 2026 volume lapses, so EPS falls below FY2026E before growing again.

base.driver: EBITDA grows inside the 4-8% medium-term range; buybacks (2.6bn of the 6bn program done by 26 Oct 2026) and lower interest lift EPS faster than EBITDA, but FX and the 2026 World Cup boost do not repeat, leaving about 5.6% EPS growth on FY2026E.

bull.driver: Premiumisation and emerging-market pricing sustain the top of the 4-8% EBITDA range, and the market keeps paying a premium multiple for visible cash returns.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $4.70 the $84.81 close implies 18.0x (19.1x on FY2026E of $4.45). The MarketBeat consensus target of $87.83 (25 Oct 2026, 12 Buy and 4 Hold) implies 18.7x on $4.70, or about $4.97 of EPS at 18x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $4.70 (about 5.5 pp of the close); a $0.10 change in FY2027 EPS moves it by $1.80 (about 2.1 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Normalised EBITDA growth against the 4-8% range (9M26 was +5.0% at $17,332M), together with the company's initial 2027 EPS or EBITDA framing and the Brazil sin tax impact on volumes and pricing.
valuation.next_disclosure: FY2026 results with initial 2027 outlook, expected around mid-February 2027 (date not confirmed; FY2025 results were released 12 Feb 2026).

analyst_notes: Only one named call could be sourced with a date before the close: Laurence Whyatt at Barclays cut the EUR target from 95 to 82 and moved to Equal Weight on 27 Jul 2026, citing the 2027 Brazil sin tax and a premium valuation. Firm-only actions (Wells Fargo cut to $88 from $97 on 5 Oct 2026, TD Cowen cut to $85 from $89 on 13 Oct 2026 with a Hold, RBC raised to EUR 95 from EUR 93 on 8 Oct 2026, and others) have no named analyst in the sources, so they are excluded from the named timeline and from the weighted target. The MarketBeat consensus of $87.83 sits 3.5% above the close and about $4.97 of FY2027 EPS at 18x, above the base case, so the gap is mostly a difference in 2027 earnings assumptions rather than in multiple; no named target carries a documented 12-month horizon.
